doc.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001

title: Hatred, religion and peacemakers
summary: Asked how the present conflict might be resolved, Brubeck points to loving one's enemy, Buddha, and Malcolm X's change after Mecca.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: In this current situation we’re in now, with different philosophies and different religions involved, can you see a way to best resolve what’s going on?

Yeah but we’ve waited so long that hatred is so entrenched and false explanation to all the religious groups of what the religion really stands for. If you got to the basis of, for instance, Buddha 600 years before Christ, said, “the crowning enlightenment is to love your enemy.” And that may be where Christ picked that up. And when Malcolm X went © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-

to Mecca he changed his whole philosophy when he got back to the United States. He said you know we’re all going in — not all, but we’re stating a lot of things that aren’t true about Islam. And he was silenced for being a peacemaker.
Yeah. Trying to change the course of what some of his other people wanted.
